# x86_semantics.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/integer-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 9V45 (raven-macos-bench run 44527495718, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 112983216c7f89c2a25eb2714acebcbf2025c311fef7b23b2370060e2bd51f9b): every family, bit scan and strings the newest. The tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change.
# Earlier runs gave the same results for the families they had: AMD EPYC 9V74 runs 44522174773 (random) and 44522713416 (random, multiply, divide), AMD EPYC 7763 runs 44523646082 (and bit test) and 44524257886 (and locked), AMD EPYC 9V45 run 44526496471 (and group 4). The random family's one difference, the RAX a 32-bit lock cmpxchg leaves, was first found on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (run 44411803673).
# Rosetta and the EPYCs agree in every register, memory byte and defined flag of every directed family; they differ only in flags x86 leaves undefined (counted by silicon_overrides.py, not written).
